items.title: UKMTO reports new tanker strike while ADNOC confirms damage to a vessel
items.summary: UKMTO Warning 201-26 reports a tanker struck by an unknown projectile 19 nautical miles northeast of Lima, Oman, with crew safe and no reported pollution. ADNOC Logistics & Services separately confirmed attack damage to one of its vessels in UAE waters. Whether these refer to the same ship, the attacker, and any incremental oil-flow loss remain unverified.

items.title: Anthropic files IPO price range and $26 billion strategic partner placement
items.summary: Anthropic's November 10 S-1 amendment sets a proposed 825 million-share IPO at $70–$78 per share, including existing-holder shares. Seven chip and cloud partners agreed to purchase $26 billion of non-voting stock in a concurrent private placement, subject to closing conditions. The filing underscores major AI-compute financing needs while valuation and capital efficiency remain unresolved.

items.title: SoftBank takes $3.7 billion data-center power-equipment charge as GE Vernova shares fall
items.summary: SoftBank disclosed a $3.7 billion charge after revising procurement plans for U.S. AI-data-center power equipment. GE Vernova fell about 6.8% in Tuesday morning trading amid concerns about future gas-turbine orders. SoftBank said the charge was unrelated to its Ports-Pike campus; the specific affected suppliers have not been confirmed.

items.title: Qualys drops sharply despite earnings beat as forward calculated billings slow
items.summary: Qualys reported Q3 revenue of $188 million and adjusted EPS of $2.12, beating consensus, but guided to approximately 8% Q4 calculated current billings growth versus 14% in Q3. Shares were down 12.36% at a 12:37 PM EST market observation. Full-year revenue guidance increased; whether billings deceleration persists is the critical fundamental test.

items.title: EIA projects persistent diesel and tanker tightness despite November oil-price slide
items.summary: EIA's November 10 outlook raised its 2027 U.S. diesel price forecast by 12% to $5.03/gallon and expects Brent around $100/barrel in November–December. It estimates October Middle East shut-in production at 2.5 million barrels/day, down from 10.9 million at May's peak. Forecast inputs were finalized November 5 and exclude subsequent diplomatic developments and oil-price declines.
